title: InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator constructor lacks stakedId/stakedToken cross-check — strandable parked principal on owner mis-wire
description: InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator's constructor wires the source and destination stakers without asserting that their stakedId / stakedToken parameters are mutually consistent. If the owner mis-wires the migrator with mismatched staked token / staked id configuration, principal parked in the migrator during migration can be stranded.
impact: On an owner mis-wire, parked principal can become strandable mid-migration. Non-obvious deploy-time configuration footgun (Law-3 in-scope hazard). No attacker, no theft; recoverable/avoidable with a correct deploy. Low severity.
attackPath: No attacker. Trigger is a deploy-time owner mis-wire of the migrator.
1. Owner deploys InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator with mismatched stakedId/stakedToken vs the source/destination stakers.
2. Constructor does not assert config consistency, so the mis-wire is accepted silently.
3. Principal parked in the migrator during migration can be stranded under the inconsistent wiring.
recommendation: Add a constructor assertion that the migrator's stakedId/stakedToken match the configured source and destination stakers (e.g. require source.stakedToken() == dest.stakedToken() && source.stakedId() == dest.stakedId()), so a mis-wire reverts at deploy time instead of stranding principal at migration time.
category: QA/Low operational footgun (Law-3 non-obvious deploy-time configuration hazard)
